name.text: Reflection and tessellation - predict the fish colour (Escher)

questiontext.text:
Inspired by artist M.C Escher's drawings, in the diagram below four mirrors (blue dashed) at \(x=\pm m\) and \(y=\pm k\) surround four coloured fish. Press Reflect to reflect everything across the four walls. It stops one reflection short of the green target \(\times\): the fish that will cover the target is not drawn.

What colour will the fish be that covers the target \(\times\) on the next reflection?

generalfeedback.text:
Reflecting the motif makes a lattice of congruent fish. The colour follows a perfect colouring: each mirror you cross flips the colour in a fixed way, so a fish's colour is settled by how many mirrors separate it from the motif.

Below, the pattern is drawn at the last step before the target. The purple-outlined fish is the mirror image of the target — the same distance from the mirror, on the same row — and it folds across onto the target. Press Reflect to reflect it over and reveal the colour — {@colourword@}.

node.description: Chosen colour equals the target fish's colour?

truefeedback.text: Correct. You can find a fish this colour as the target an identical distance across the mirror.

falsefeedback.text: Not quite. How far away is the target from each of the mirrors? Which colour fish has the same distance to the mirror as the target?
